differences.title: 1. REQUEST PIPELINE
differences.leftDesc: Django runs requests through a well-defined middleware chain, resolves URLs via URLconf, then dispatches to class-based or function views, using the request/response objects and thread-local state for context.
differences.rightDesc: FastAPI builds on ASGI and executes endpoints as async callables. It wires inputs with a dependency graph (Depends), then validates, runs user code, and serializes responses with minimal overhead.

differences.title: 2. DATA VALIDATION
differences.leftDesc: Django typically validates using forms, model constraints, and manual serializers. Errors surface through form/model validation flows, often tightly coupled to ORM types and field-level clean methods.
differences.rightDesc: FastAPI uses Pydantic for automatic request parsing and validation. Type hints drive schema generation, coercion, and error responses, including nested models and constrained fields with clear 422 payloads.

differences.title: 3. TYPE-DRIVEN DOCS
differences.leftDesc: Django documentation is often produced manually or via add-ons. Because Django views aren’t primarily type-annotated for request/response schemas, schema accuracy depends on extra tooling and conventions.
differences.rightDesc: FastAPI generates OpenAPI specs automatically from Python type hints and Pydantic models. It produces interactive Swagger UI and ReDoc that stay synchronized with runtime validation and response models.

differences.title: 4. PERFORMANCE MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Django’s core request handling is largely synchronous, optimized for the traditional WSGI ecosystem. Async support exists, but many stacks (middleware/ORM usage) can still impose sync boundaries.
differences.rightDesc: FastAPI is designed for ASGI concurrency, making it easier to run async endpoints that release the event loop during I/O. This can improve throughput for network-bound workloads with fewer threads.

differences.title: 5. ORM COUPLING
differences.leftDesc: Django heavily encourages an ORM-centric approach: models define schema, migrations, and relationships. Views frequently operate with ORM querysets and model validation patterns.
differences.rightDesc: FastAPI does not prescribe a persistence layer. You can pair it with SQLAlchemy, databases, or async drivers, keeping endpoint logic focused on request/response while you control ORM/transaction boundaries.

differences.title: 6. AUTH & SECURITY EXTENSION
differences.leftDesc: Django includes a mature authentication/authorization system (sessions, permissions, middleware integration). Common security flows are standardized through its auth apps and admin-friendly patterns.
differences.rightDesc: FastAPI typically implements auth using dependency injection. You can enforce security scopes per-route by composing dependencies, and integrate JWT/OAuth logic while retaining explicit control over guards.

differences.title: 7. ECOSYSTEM SHAPE
differences.leftDesc: Django’s ecosystem provides a cohesive, batteries-included full-stack framework: templating, admin, ORM, migrations, and conventions that reduce integration work but increase framework surface area.
differences.rightDesc: FastAPI’s core is intentionally API-first and lightweight, emphasizing request handling, validation, and documentation. You assemble additional pieces (DB, auth, background jobs) based on your architecture needs.
